facts.fact: The Interior Ministry's deputy secretary-general said at Tahoua on 11 August 2026 that the national civil-status system belongs to the ministry's Direction Générale de l'état civil, des Migrations et des Réfugiés, which is to receive the investments for computerising communes and declaration centres, a new platform and the Registre National d'État Civil (RNEC); the ANEI is to administer the RNP and its underlying registers.
facts.system: nouvelle plateforme de gestion des faits d'état civil

facts.fact: The investments announced on 11 August 2026 for civil-status computerisation are presented under the WURI-Niger project, which the ANP states is financed by the World Bank and under the Interior Minister's oversight; no domestic budget line is mentioned.
facts.system: nouvelle plateforme de gestion des faits d'état civil

facts.fact: The deputy secretary-general said on 11 August 2026 that Axis 2 of the Programme pour la Refondation de la République 2025-2029 gives an important place to modernising civil status; the programme is not reported as naming the platform or as costed.
facts.system: nouvelle plateforme de gestion des faits d'état civil

facts.fact: On 11 August 2026 the Interior Ministry announced, as short- and medium-term prospects not yet delivered, the computerisation of all communes and declaration centres, the putting into service of a new, more sovereign and more secure platform for managing civil-status events, and the operationalisation of an RNEC.
facts.system: nouvelle plateforme de gestion des faits d'état civil
